moneyMovementGoNoGo.reason: FIND-001 (CRITICAL, this iteration): the sole value-moving Base transaction's four-gate verifyEvmTxAgainstIntent check (the iter1 FIND-001/002 fix) closes the BARE-transfer whole-balance-drain vector but does not close a narrower, still-severe vector: a fully-malicious/compromised Skip route response can cause this module to sign a transaction whose actual on-chain execution pulls up to APPROVAL_CAP_BASE_UNITS ($100) via an already-standing ERC-20 allowance to a route-supplied spender contract, regardless of the driver's independently-capped, much smaller `amount` (max $20, SWAP_MAX_USD). This is because gate 3 only cross-checks a SELF-REPORTED metadata field in Skip's HTTP response against the intended amount -- it never decodes evm_tx.data to verify what the target contract's own logic will actually pull, and the on-chain allowance itself was set (in a PRIOR, separate approve() call from getNextNonce()) to a fixed $100 ceiling independent of any specific swap's amount, and is never lowered/revoked between swaps. Answer to the reviewer-crux question: loss under a fully-malicious Skip route is NOT bounded to `amount` -- it is bounded to $100 (a real, quantifiable, 5x-of-intended-amount loss ceiling), which is bounded (not whole-balance) but is neither claimed as an accepted risk anywhere in the spec/verification-architecture nor actually mitigated by the code's own doc comments' claims. Recommend (not prescriptive): either (a) decode evm_tx.data for the entry-point-call path and independently verify the encoded pull amount against `amount` (closing the gap at its root), and/or (b) stop maintaining a standing $100 allowance across swaps -- approve exactly `amount` per swap and let it be consumed, so the on-chain allowance itself (not a self-reported metadata field) is the thing that structurally equals the intended amount every time. Until one of these lands, a real Base->Akash swap should not be run against a Skip endpoint whose integrity cannot be fully trusted (TLS MITM, Skip-side compromise, or a Skip-side bug returning a wrong spender/calldata pairing).
